conventions: TypeScript strict, ESM, Prettier via ESLint: 2 spaces, double quotes, trailing commas, 80 columns. `yarn test:code` runs with --max-warnings=0.
Type imports are separate `import type` statements (consistent-type-imports). Keep import/order: external and @excalidraw/* first, then parent, then sibling, then type imports.

Inside packages/element import siblings relatively (./textRanges). Inside packages/excalidraw import element code from "@excalidraw/element", types from "@excalidraw/element/types", and never through a packages/excalidraw barrel.
New DOM use goes through app.ownerDocument / app.ownerWindow, or the ownerDocument of a mounted node. Never use the global document in new code.
Prefer immutable data. Range arrays and range objects are never mutated in place: every change builds new objects (delta.ts compares entries by identity).
A style-only change goes through newElementWith or a spread, never through mutateElement: mutateElement keeps the same object, so elementWithCanvasCache would paint stale text.
New element fields get a JSDoc block in types.ts. Comments state why, not what, and stay short.

Tests run on Vitest with globals, jsdom and vitest-canvas-mock. Use API, UI, Keyboard, getTextEditor, updateTextEditor and act from the existing helpers. Assert with expect; no toMatchSnapshot and no new snapshot files anywhere.
In the test env getLineWidth returns text.length * 10, so x and width values in tests are exact multiples of 10.
UI strings go through t("labels.x") and live in packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json only. Every other locale file is Crowdin's.

decisions.choice: Run constraint: work only from this branch's code and the brief. Do not look at the upstream excalidraw repo, its PRs or issues, upstream/master or master, and do not base anything on them. This binds every phase and every model, the Gemini worker included.
decisions.reason: The person's Gate 0 answer, word for word.

decisions.choice: Concurrent edits: keep your reading of "survive" and do not narrow the brief to last-write-wins. The losing version's ranges are carried onto the winning text, no client shows stale offsets, all clients converge whichever order they receive versions in, and a removed range does not come back.
rejected: Last-write-wins on the whole element or on the textRanges key
decisions.reason: The person's Gate 0 answer.

decisions.choice: ExcalidrawTextElement gets one optional key `textRanges?: ExcalidrawTextRanges` = { textHash: number; ranges: ExcalidrawTextRange[] }. textHash is hashString(originalText). A range is { id, start, end, z, color?, highlight?, retired?, origin? }: start and end are half-open UTF-16 offsets into originalText; id is randomId() and encodes no user, client or device; z is the layer; color and highlight are a colour string (sets it), null (clears it) or absent (leaves it alone). id, z, color and highlight never change after a range is created.
rejected: Two top-level keys (ranges plus a tombstone list), which history would apply separately
One range per attribute with a kind field: FR-1 says colour and/or highlight on one range
decisions.reason: One replaced value keeps text offsets and their hash together. Anchoring to originalText means a re-wrap alone never changes offsets (FR-1).

decisions.topic: Key absent by default (FR-2 as revised at Gate 1)
decisions.choice: An element that has NEVER had ranges carries no textRanges key, in memory or on save: newTextElement does not set it, restore never adds it, and a colour or reset that changes no visible style leaves it absent. An element whose ranges were all removed keeps its textRanges container as the marker FR-19 needs: clear, retired and collapsed records stay in it.
decisions.reason: Keeps every existing snapshot and legacy file byte-identical, and gives a removal something to travel in.

decisions.topic: Layers: how one style is decided per character (FR-4)
decisions.choice: Ranges are layers, not disjoint segments. A style operation never rewrites an existing range's span: it adds one record on top with z = 1 + the highest z in the element. A colour pick adds { color } and touches nothing else, a highlight pick adds { highlight }, Reset adds { color: null, highlight: null }. A style with a null is a removal and also retires what it touches (see Removal and tombstones). For each attribute separately, the style of a character comes from the covering, non-retired record with that attribute present, ordered by highest z, then null before a string at equal z, then highest id. getTextStyleRuns is the only reader of this order and returns disjoint runs. Stored records of one attribute may overlap, because a style operation never shrinks a record.
rejected: Disjoint records with no clear on top: two clients each removing half of a range would keep each other's remainder, so the whole range would come back
Per-range revision counters: they cannot express a partial removal
decisions.reason: A grow-only set of immutable records is a join under union, which is what makes merging order-independent, and a partial removal survives because a clear is a record like any other.

decisions.choice: Text edits map offsets through diffText hunks. Insertion strictly inside a range extends it. Insertion exactly at a range's start shifts it and is not included. Insertion exactly at a range's end leaves it alone and is not included. A replacement overlapping a boundary leaves the inserted text outside the range. Deletion shrinks a range. A range whose characters are all deleted stays in the list collapsed (start === end) and native (no origin): it styles nothing from then on, and typing the same text again never reopens it, because mapStart(p) >= mapEnd(p) keeps a collapsed span collapsed. Its id is what stops a merge re-adding it from a peer's copy. Where repeated text lets an insertion or a deletion sit at a word edge and not inside the word, the final diff pass puts it at the edge, so these rules read it there.
rejected: Extending a range when typing at its end: it would also extend every clear, so typing after a removed word would change what was removed
Dropping a range whose characters are all deleted: a peer then holds an id the base does not, so the merge re-adds it with the old text in origin, and retyping the word turns it red again
decisions.reason: One rule for start and one for end, used by the editor, list markers, history and carrying, so a range and a clear over it always move together.

decisions.topic: Merged element's version and nonce (FR-19, FR-20, NFR-3)
decisions.choice: reconcileElements picks the base exactly as today (shouldDiscardRemoteElement is unchanged and still exported). The merged element is { ...base, textRanges: merged }: inside reconcileElements it keeps the base's version, versionNonce, updated and every other field. Both clients call mergeTextRanges(base = the same winner, other = the same loser), so two clients with the same two versions compute the same element (NFR-3). If the merged ranges equal the base's, the base object itself is returned. In the app, Collab._reconcileElements then runs bumpElementVersions(reconciled, existing) (Collab.tsx:790, unchanged). After reconcile it fires in one case only: the client took a remote element at an equal version with a different nonce. That element gets version + 1, a fresh random versionNonce and a new updated, and nothing else holds that version and nonce. So after an equal-version race the client whose own element won holds the winner's version and nonce, the client that took the remote holds the bumped ones, and the two are equal in every other field, originalText and textRanges included. A higher-version winner is not bumped, so in that race both clients match on every field at once. Nothing rebroadcasts at that moment: Collab sets lastBroadcastedOrReceivedSceneVersion from the bumped total, so broadcastElements sees nothing newer. The next delivery ends the difference: the receiver takes the higher version, the merge returns it unchanged, no bump fires because the local version is lower, and both clients match on every field. mergeTextRanges also runs when version and nonce are equal, so a client still holding the un-merged winner picks up the merged ranges from a full sync. Two clients that both took the remote in one race hold the same version with different nonces and equal content: their next exchange is an ordinary equal-version race, one bumps once more, and the delivery after that ends it, as for every element today.
rejected: Bumping the version inside the merge: two clients with the same two versions would compute different elements (NFR-3), and elements with no ranges must reconcile as today
Deriving a new nonce from a hash of the merged state: the nonce is the tie-break, so it would change the winner
decisions.reason: Base fields are a last-write-wins register and the range table is a union, and the product of two joins is a join: commutative, associative and idempotent, so arrival order cannot matter. Collab's bump sits outside that join and behaves like one more local version with the same content, so it delays field-for-field equality by one delivery and cannot change what clients converge to.

decisions.topic: Carrying ranges onto the winning text (FR-19)
decisions.choice: Each record has a position register, a value compared as (higher version, then lower versionNonce). A record's register is its `origin` field if present, else { version, versionNonce, text: originalText, start, end } of the element holding it. If the base holds the id with no origin, the base's offsets win. Otherwise the newest register among the two sides is mapped onto the base's text through diffText(register.text, base.originalText, meter) and mapSpanThroughHunks, as the Diff budget decision states, and stored as the record's origin, unchanged. The mapping always starts from the register's own text, never from an intermediate merged text, so carrying through any number of merges gives the same offsets as carrying directly. A carried record whose characters are gone in the base stays in the list collapsed (start === end) with its origin, because a later winning text may still hold them. Any local edit (a style op or a text edit) makes every record native again by dropping origin. A bump never touches origin. A native record on a bumped element takes the bumped version and nonce as its register, with the same text and offsets, so it maps to the same place: two clients can hold different origin fields for a record until the next delivery, the newer register wins that delivery, and their offsets agree throughout.
rejected: Common prefix and suffix only: when both ends of a text changed, everything in the middle would be lost
Mapping from the previous merged text: path-dependent once three versions race
Finding the styled substring by search: a word edited on the winning side would lose its range
decisions.reason: offsets = f(register, winning text) is a pure function of two joined values, which is the only way three-way races stay order-independent with no common ancestor.

decisions.choice: A removal of a selection (Reset, or the transparent highlight swatch) does three things. It retires, by id, every record it touches all of whose string attributes it clears, whether it covers that record fully or partly, so no text path can bring any of that record back. For a record it covers only partly, it adds the part outside the selection as a fresh record at the same z (a kept part). It adds a clear record on top, which hides every lower layer over that span, stays in the list, and is carried like any other record. Two clients each clearing part of a range hide all of it, because each one's kept part lies under the other's clear. A colour edit racing a removal at the same z loses to the removal. A range created at a higher z by a client that had not seen the removal is a different range and stays. `retired: true` is the id tombstone: it is written by a removal and by undoing a style step, it is sticky under merge (logical OR), and a retired id is never revived. Undoing a removal and redoing a style step both re-add the style under a fresh id at its own z, so the layer order comes back as it was. retired records keep shifting with the text, because those re-adds read their offsets.
rejected: A clear alone: the record stays alive on the peer's offsets, so a clear carried by a different diff path lands one character off at a repeated character and a sliver of the removed range shows
Retiring only records the removal fully covers: a partly covered record stays alive on the peer's offsets, so the same sliver shows at its outer edge
decisions.reason: With no common ancestor, reconcile can only tell removal from not-yet-seen by a record that is present. A clear or a retired record is that record, and an id is the one thing a diff cannot misplace.

decisions.topic: Known limit: the remaining edge of a carried removal
decisions.choice: A record a removal touched never shows again, whichever way a diff resolves a repeated character, because it is out by id. Exactly three things remain, and each needs a race. (1) The boundary between a clear and its kept part is placed by one diffText between the remover's text and the winning text. If the winning side changed a run of repeated characters or a repeated substring at that boundary, the kept part can sit to one side of where the keystrokes put it, or lose characters, by up to the amount of text the winning side added or removed there. (2) A clear hides a record its author had not seen, such as a colour made in the same race or another client's kept part, by position only. If that record and the clear reached the winning text by different paths, and the winning side changed repeated text at the clear's edge, that record can show beside the clear by the same amount. (3) If one client undoes a style step while another partly removes the same range, the kept part stays, because undo writes no clear.
decisions.reason: The person asked at Gate 2 to close this or state it. Case 1 cannot be closed from text alone: repeated characters have no identity and reconcile sees no keystrokes. Cases 2 and 3 concern records the remover never saw, so they cannot be retired by id.

decisions.choice: While shouldDiscardRemoteElement drops a remote update because the local user edits that element (also while resizing or creating it), the update's text and every non-range field are discarded as today. Its ranges are NOT discarded: reconcileElements calls mergeTextRanges(local, remote), so each of its records, including clears and retired flags, joins the local element at once, mapped onto the local text, keeping the local version and nonce. The preview redraws from the scene update, and offsets address the text in the editor, so nothing is stale. Local records win position over remote for any id they hold natively. When editing ends nothing special runs: the local version is broadcast as usual if typing bumped it, and the next delivery of either version merges through the ordinary path to the same element on both clients, whichever wins on version. The discard branch never bumps, and a tie after editing ends takes Collab's bump as any equal-version race does.
rejected: Holding the dropped update aside and replaying it at submit: it needs local state outside the element, which NFR-3 rules out of the merge
Bumping the version at submit past the dropped update: it changes reconcile for no range reason and elements with no ranges must reconcile as today
decisions.reason: reconcileElements keeps its signature and stays pure, and FR-21's three demands are met by the same merge as FR-19.

decisions.choice: textRanges is never written straight from a delta. ElementsDelta.applyDelta calls applyTextRangesDelta, which starts from the element's current records, shifts them to the delta's text if the delta holds originalText, then applies the difference between the delta's two sides by id: an id alive in the delta's deleted side and not in its inserted side is retired; an id alive in the inserted side and not in the deleted side is re-added, under a fresh id at its own z if its current record is retired. Offsets from a delta are used only when that delta also restores originalText and the element's current text equals the delta's deleted text, or when a record is collapsed on both the element and the delta's deleted side and the delta's inserted ranges address the resulting text, which is how undoing the step that lost a word brings its range back too. Undoing a range step after a remote text edit therefore keeps offsets on the current text. Undo and redo are forward operations: they merge with peers like any edit.
rejected: Replacing textRanges from the delta: a peer's union would bring an undone record back, and offsets would go stale after an interleaved remote text edit
decisions.reason: Delta applies only the keys it holds, so a separate range key must be reconciled with the current text at apply time.

decisions.topic: Known limit: undo after a same-version merge
decisions.choice: StoreSnapshot detects change by a rising version (store.ts:935), so a merge that keeps the version does not refresh the store snapshot. That is the client whose own element won, or who is editing, resizing or creating it, in reconcile's discard branch. A client that took the remote has a rising version, through the winner's higher version or Collab's bump, and its snapshot is current, so the limit does not reach it. On the discard-branch client, the next local edit's history step also spans records carried in by that merge. Undoing that one step retires those records, and a range a peer removed in that merge shows again, under a fresh id. Offsets stay valid and clients still converge. No workaround is written; packages/element/src/store.ts is outside the allowlist.
decisions.reason: A merge must not raise a version inside reconcile (NFR-3). The limit needs a race the local element won, then a local edit, then an undo of that exact step.

decisions.topic: Known limit: overlap is not repaired at restore
decisions.choice: Overlap between stored records is not malformed (FR-18). It stays as stored, in memory, in files and on the wire, and only getTextStyleRuns resolves it, by the fixed layer order. A saved element can therefore hold records that no character shows.
decisions.reason: Overlap is the normal output of FR-4 and of merging. Flattening it would rewrite join state.

decisions.topic: Known limit: deleted text in origin.text
decisions.choice: origin.text holds the losing version's full text, so after a concurrent-edit race text deleted on one client can stay in that element, in memory, in saves and on the wire, until the next style action or text edit on that element. Only a race writes it: a merge sets origin only when the base does not hold the id or holds it carried. A deletion with no race keeps the record collapsed and native, so it leaves no old text in the element on either client.
decisions.reason: Carrying needs the register's own text, and any local edit drops it. This matches the PII line in requirements.md.

decisions.topic: Known limit: convergence waits for the next delivery
decisions.choice: FR-19 holds once each client has received the other's latest version, not at the moment of a race. No client ever shows stale offsets meanwhile. Until then a bumped client differs from the other in version, versionNonce and updated, and if only one direction was delivered, the receiver holds merged records the sender lacks. Neither sends anything because of that. The next delivery is that client's next broadcast of any scene change, the full sync that follows a broadcast (SYNC_FULL_SCENE_INTERVAL_MS, 20 s, queued only by a broadcast), or a Firebase save by either client, which reconciles the stored scene back in. No timer forces one, so a quiet room stays in that state. Firebase: isSavedToFirebase compares the sum of versions, so a merge with no version rise does not make that client save. A client that took a remote element has a higher sum and saves, and saveToFirebase's own reconcileElements merges against the stored scene. So the stored scene lacks a merged record only if that client left before its throttled save ran, and then the winner's next version rise stores it.
decisions.reason: excalidraw-app/** does not change, and these are today's delivery rules for every element.

decisions.choice: Ctrl+Z inside the textarea is the browser's own, because App's key handler bails inside a writable element. It changes text only, and FR-16 treats that as any other edit: a colour applied in the session is not undone by it, and a word it brings back stays unstyled, because that word's record stays collapsed. The app's undo after leaving the editor restores text and ranges together.
decisions.reason: The textarea stays (FR-15), and its undo stack is not ours to change.

decisions.topic: Known limit: canvas bidi model and Arabic shaping
decisions.choice: On a line with a visible run, layoutTextLine splits the line into ltr and rtl segments by a simple strong-character model, not the full Unicode bidi algorithm, so a mixed-direction line can place runs differently from the same unstyled line. Each canvas piece is its own fillText, so a run boundary inside an Arabic word breaks letter joining at that boundary. SVG text keeps one <text> per line, so the browser shapes and orders it, but SVG highlight rects use the same layout. Lines with no visible run take today's path, with context.direction set back to the element's direction, because the line before may have left a piece's direction on the context.
decisions.reason: The canvas has no API for shaping across fillText calls, and jsdom cannot test a fuller model.

decisions.topic: Known limit: the compact panel's Background title
decisions.choice: The highlight picker has type elementBackground, and Picker.tsx titles its popup by type when showTitle is set, which ColorPicker does in compact mode. So in the compact and mobile panels the open popup reads "Background". The trigger's title and aria-label are right. Picker.tsx is outside the allowlist.
decisions.reason: A cosmetic label in one mode, and the scope cannot change in this run.

decisions.choice: MAX_TEXT_RANGES = 1024 records per element, counting retired, clear, collapsed and kept-part records. canonicalizeTextRanges keeps the highest (z, id), so past the cap the lowest layers are dropped, identically on every client, and that styling disappears. Records never leave the list otherwise, and a removal adds its clear plus up to two kept parts per touched record, so a heavily restyled element reaches the cap sooner than its visible runs suggest. A dropped record cannot return from a peer, because the merged list is cut the same way.
decisions.reason: NFR-2 needs a bound on stored records, and a grow-only list has no other.

decisions.topic: Text diff mechanism (FR-3, FR-16, FR-19, NFR-2, NFR-3, Gate 4)
decisions.choice: diffText no longer fills a table and no longer falls back at a cell cap; MAX_DIFF_CELLS is gone. Everything is in packages/element/src/textDiff.ts, and diffText stays the one function shiftTextRanges and mergeTextRanges share. It searches before it trims. A queue of gaps starts with the two whole texts. Each gap takes its longest common run of at least MIN_MATCH_LENGTH (3) characters, which splits it into a left and a right gap, breadth-first. An index of oldText's 3-character grams finds the runs: a flat Int32Array table sized to the text, not a Map. In a gap the search starts at the middle of the gap's new text and moves outward, so that of runs of equal length the one nearest the middle wins and a repetitive note splits in half each time. It steps by the best length so far minus 1, because a longer run must hold a whole gram at one of those positions. At each position it tries at most MAX_MATCH_CANDIDATES (16) old positions, nearest the gap's own diagonal first. The longer of the common prefix and common suffix is the first gap's starting best, so a run must be strictly longer to beat it: a tie stays where trimming put it, and a change that repeats text beside it behaves as before. When the search ends, only the first and last gaps are trimmed of a common prefix and suffix, which keeps short matches at the text's two ends as before. A change of fewer than MIN_MATCH_LENGTH characters in total skips the search, so typing one character costs only the trim and gives the hunk it gave before. A block never starts or ends inside a surrogate pair. Every step charges a DiffMeter, and when the meter runs out the search stops and keeps what it has found (see Diff budget per merge). Repeated text has no identity: when two copies of a run are equally long, a range follows the one this search reaches first, and only the person typing knows which copy they meant. The hunks the search leaves then go through refineHunks, the final diff pass, which has its own decision below.
rejected: Raising the cell cap: the second cause is under the cap, so a larger cap does nothing for it
Myers or any other minimal edit script: a minimal script still matches the original's letters inside added text, so runs fragment and the anchor is lost
Tokenising into words first: generated text has no words, and the brief needs both
Anchoring only on grams unique to both texts: repeated lines and repeated paragraphs have none
Scanning each gap left to right: on tied runs it peels one block per pass, so repeated lines spend the budget one line at a time
Sliding only the first and last hunks after a trim: a word of two letters left after the trim cannot anchor, so "Bid" to "Before Bid after" still loses the word
A Map as the gram index: it was slower per reconcile on the forged element than a flat Int32Array table
decisions.reason: There are three causes, not two, and this covers all of them. First, a cell cap fell back to one hunk once the two changes were far apart. Second, the eager backtrack matched the original's letters inside added text, the runs fragmented, and MIN_MATCH_LENGTH dropped them. Third: a common prefix or suffix took letters the addition shares with the word, so the insertion landed inside the word and the range widened over the added text. Searching before trimming closed that only where the suffix run beats the prefix run or the word is the whole text, as in "Bid" to "Before Bid". The Gate 4 review found it still open on "foo Bid" to "foo Before Bid", and getSlide in the final diff pass is what closes it. All figures here are from the final code, on a scratch bundle under node, never on a project file. A word changed at each end at 1,010, 1,100 and 1,500 characters keeps every word (162 of 162, 177 of 177, 243 of 243). Tab on all lines of 468, 1,054 and 1,407 characters keeps every word (82, 182 and 243). U30 pins Tab at 1,054 and 1,407 and Shift+Tab at 1,126 and 1,503 through the real editor, on prose, and the same on digits at 1,061, 1,415, 1,133 and 1,511. 100 and 333 characters on each side of the label keep all 4 words; 333 on each side of the 326-character paragraph keeps all 53. mapTextSpan(digits.slice(5000, 5100), digits, 10, 20) is { start: 5010, end: 5020 }. Scripted random edits, 66 cells of prose, code and list text from 800 to 30,000 characters with 3 to 100 edits and six kinds of edit, 25 trials each: of 3,523,451 words no edit touched, at least 99.91% land exactly in every cell. Over all cells 144 land on another copy of the same word, 30 widen over a repeated word, 19 collapse and 2 land elsewhere. 20,000 fuzzed cases, half with emoji: hunks always rebuild the new text and stay in order, and no hunk edge falls inside a surrogate pair. The work is a pure function of the two texts and the meter, and uses no clock, randomness or module state (NFR-3). Work follows repetition, and past the budget Tab loses words, as the Known limit on the budget records: 100,016 characters of unique lines used 1,868,676 units in 10.9 ms and kept all 1,785 lines, and 1,000 of one 19-character line (19,999 characters) used 1,209,258 units and kept all 1,000, but 1,000 of one 75-character line (74,999 characters) kept 8 of 1,000.

decisions.topic: Final diff pass: refineHunks (FR-3, FR-16, FR-19, Gate 4 review)
decisions.choice: refineHunks in packages/element/src/textDiff.ts is the last step of diffText. It was added after the Gate 4 review, from that review's two major findings. It was not in this plan's earlier design. It fixes two defects. First, a kept token with no 3-character anchor collapsed: "OK" to "Not OK at all", "v2" to "release v2 now", and Tab on a note of one-character lines. Second, an addition beside a word landed inside it and the range widened over the added text: "foo Bid" to "foo Before Bid" styled "Before Bid". When it runs: on the hunks the search leaves, on the trimmed hunk when the search found no block, and on the trimmed hunk when either text is under MIN_MATCH_LENGTH characters. It does not run for equal texts, for a change of under MIN_MATCH_LENGTH characters in total, or when the meter cannot pay for the index, because those return first. First loop, over the hunks: a hunk passes through when meter.left <= 0 or when either of its sides is empty. Otherwise it charges oldLength + newLength, once, and tries alignLines, then alignToken. alignLines needs both sides of the hunk to hold the same number of lines, at least 2. It gives one hunk per line pair, trimmed at both ends, so a one-character line keeps its place on Tab. alignToken needs an old side of 1 or 2 characters that is not all whitespace, has a word edge on both sides, and sits against a longer new side. It takes the first copy of that token in the new side with a word edge on both sides and no split surrogate pair, and replaces the hunk with the two insertions around that copy. Hunks empty on both sides are then dropped. Second loop, over what is left: a pure insertion or deletion, while meter.left > 0, charges its own length once and calls getSlide, and every other hunk is left alone. getSlide does nothing unless the hunk's place in the other text is inside a word. Otherwise it tries one step left, then one step right, up to the hunk's length, moving only while the text repeats and only inside the neighbouring hunks, and takes the first place outside a word that splits no surrogate pair. A word character is /[\p{L}\p{N}]/u tested on one UTF-16 unit, so an astral letter does not count as one. Past the budget neither loop does anything: the lines of a gap the search never reached are not aligned, which is why Tab loses them.
decisions.reason: Both defects hit an ordinary edit with no race, on characters that are all still there, against FR-3. Each step is pure and charged to the one meter, so NFR-3 and the budget hold, and each does work linear in the hunk it was charged for. Taking the first word-edged copy and trying left before right make every result a fixed choice; repeated text has no identity, so no choice is more right than another. U28 and U30 pin both defects: "addition beside a word", "kept token with no 3-character anchor", and Tab on the 500-line, 200-line and five-line notes.

decisions.choice: mergeTextRanges bounds its diff work per call with one work meter, which replaces the cell budget. textDiff.ts holds the only constant, MAX_DIFF_WORK, and textRangeMerge.ts repeats none of it: MAX_MERGE_DIFF_CELLS, DIFF_TEXT_MAX_CELLS and getCoarseHunk are removed, so the two files cannot disagree. Imports: `import { MAX_DIFF_WORK, diffText, mapSpanThroughHunks } from "./textDiff";` and `import type { DiffMeter, TextHunk } from "./textDiff";`. Order, unchanged from Gate 3: after allIds, `const survivors = canonicalizeTextRanges([...allIds].map((id) => (baseMap.get(id) ?? otherMap.get(id))!)).reverse();` and the loop is `for (const { id } of survivors)`, so records the MAX_TEXT_RANGES cap drops are gone before any diff runs, and the highest (z, id) is served first. Spend: before the loop, `const meter: DiffMeter = { left: MAX_DIFF_WORK };` and `const hunksByText = new Map<string, readonly TextHunk[]>();`. On a miss in hunksByText, `hunks = diffText(reg.text, base.originalText, meter);` and the result is stored under reg.text, so each distinct text is paid for once. diffText charges the meter for what it does, the final diff pass included, and stops when the meter runs out. A text it cannot pay to index costs nothing, so it does not stop a later, shorter one. `const mapped = mapSpanThroughHunks(hunks, reg.start, reg.end);` follows as before. Test, in packages/excalidraw/tests/data/reconcile.textRanges.test.ts, counts work and never times it: `vi.mock("@excalidraw/element/textDiff", ...)` wraps diffText in a vi.fn over importOriginal, cleared just before the merge, so its calls and results are visible. W is 10,000 generated characters. The winner holds 1,024 carried records with distinct 100-character origins, L1 holds one record at a higher z whose origin is W.slice(5000, 5100) with offsets [10, 20), and L2 holds three records at a lower z whose ids sort first, with distinct 100-character origins. A separate merge constant: a second number is the disagreement this round removes
A fixed price per text: a one-word edit would cost as much as a hostile text, and a fourth ordinary register would lose its diff
decisions.reason: Value: 2,000,000 work units for one merge, the same as for one local diff. The limit, with a and b the lengths of the two texts of one diffText call and n = min(a, b): that call takes the meter at most max(2n + 1, a + b - 1) below zero, which is at most a + b + 1. So one merge spends at most MAX_DIFF_WORK + a + b + 1, where a and b are those of the one diff the meter ran out on. This plan used to state MAX_DIFF_WORK + 2 * min + 2, which was wrong because it left out the final diff pass. Derivation from the code, for a diff that returns (the Open defect decision has the one that does not). The index is charged only when indexWork <= meter.left, so it leaves the meter at 0 or above. In the search every candidate is behind a read of meter.left > 0, and one candidate charges back + 1 + length, where back <= length <= n, so at most 2n + 1. From left >= 1 that leaves left >= -2n, and the second searchAt of that findLongestBlock turn charges 1 with no read before it, so the search ends at -(2n + 1) or higher. refineHunks reads meter.left before every charge, and a charge is the length of one hunk, at most a + b, so from left >= 1 it ends at -(a + b - 1) or higher. Past that one unit, nothing is charged once the meter is at or below zero: both refineHunks loops skip, and a later diff in the same merge has indexWork > 0 >= left, so it returns the trimmed hunk. So one charge crosses zero, in one diff. Proved by running it on the final code, old "0123456789" against new random letters. New 900,000: the meter ends at -729,136, from index 900,040, search 929,086, so 170,874 left when the final pass charges 900,010. Limit 900,011. New 800,000: -425,906, from index 800,040, search 825,856, so 374,104 left when the final pass charges 800,010. Limit 800,011. The old formula gave 22 for both. The overrun is linear and harmless: those two take about 10 ms. Tightest found, new 984,070: 984,062 against 984,081. 200,000 random pairs of short texts with random meters: none past max(2n + 1, a + b - 1), and none charged anything with the meter at or below zero. Outside the meter are the trim, at most 2n compares per distinct register text, so linear in the payload as before, and sorting the blocks found, each of which cost at least 4 units. Measured on 115 adversarial inputs (random text over small alphabets, periodic text, blocks of 3 characters, no match at all), with old texts up to 400,000 characters, in three runs: the slowest took 30.9 to 33 ms (25,000 blocks of 3 characters), and the largest overrun past zero was 399,998 units (300,000 characters of period 3 against its reverse, limit 600,001). Forged-element timing, one set, measured by the coordinator on the final code through real restoreElements and reconcileElements under jsdom: 1,024 records, about 254 KB of JSON, against a 10,000-character text, nine reconciles per fixture. Four text shapes, random letters, two letters, periodic text and repeated lines, each with two origin kinds, unrelated 100-character text and slices of the base. Median and worst single run in ms: random 20.3 and 31.6 unrelated, 8.7 and 12.0 slices; two letters 16.1 and 17.6 unrelated, 16.2 and 17.8 slices; periodic 12.9 and 14.0 unrelated, 12.2 and 12.6 slices; lines 12.2 and 15.7 unrelated, 9.5 and 10.5 slices. So medians run 8.7 to 20.3 ms and the worst single run was 31.6 ms. In U28's budget scenario 44 of the 1,024 diffs return several hunks before the meter runs out. An ordinary race stays under the budget: three register texts of 10,000 characters with one edit each used 120,210 units on varied text and 273,675 on one paragraph repeated to that length. Convergence: a record native to the base and a register equal to the base are not mapped and cost nothing. Every other surviving record is remapped from its own register on every merge that reaches the loop, and a merge whose other side has no records returns the base and adds none. So nothing carries spend between calls: it depends only on the base text and the registers of the surviving records, not on how a client reached them. The survivors are the same on every client, because the top MAX_TEXT_RANGES by (z, id) of a union does not depend on the order of the unions, and the cut comes before any diff. The order they are served in comes from that same canonical sort, and a partial diff is a pure function of the two texts and what the meter holds on arrival, so the result is the same however a client reached those survivors. A bumped client's native records register the base's own text, which diffText answers with no work, so a bump changes no spend. Two clients with the same two versions compute the same element (NFR-3), and the merge stays idempotent: a repeat sees the same survivors and registers, gets the same hunks and returns the base. meter and hunksByText live and die in one call, so no local-only state enters the merge.

decisions.topic: Known limit: the diff budget is per element
decisions.choice: MAX_DIFF_WORK is per diffText call for a local text edit and per element for a merge, one mergeTextRanges call, so many forged elements still add up in proportion to payload size. What really happens past the budget: a diff that cannot pay for its index returns one hunk, the text between the common prefix and the common suffix, and a diff that runs out partway keeps every block it has found and leaves each remaining gap as a hunk. A range wholly inside such a hunk collapses and styles nothing: a carried range keeps its origin, so a later merge with budget left can still place it, and a native range stays collapsed as a deleted range does, until an app undo restores it. A range with one end inside the hunk keeps only its part outside the hunk. A range that spans the whole hunk keeps both ends and also covers the hunk's new text. In a merge the highest (z, id) records are served first, so the records that lose out are the lowest layers. A text over about 400,000 characters is never indexed, since the index alone would use the budget, so an edit to it behaves like the trim: one change is exact, and a range between two far-apart changes collapses. Tab reaches this limit, the person accepted that at Gate 4 for very long notes, and the loss is silent: nothing warns, and the word just stops being styled. The cliff depends on repetition and line length, not on one size. Measured on the final code, diffText from a scratch bundle, Tab on all lines, where kept means the word stays on its true offset. One line repeated (75 characters): fine at 30,000 characters; at 40,000, 448 of 534 lines lost; at 50,000, 640 of 667; at 100,000, 1,330 of 1,334. Lines differing only by a row number: fine at 30,000; at 40,000, 351 of 478 lost; at 100,000, 1,185 of 1,190. Ten lines repeated: fine at 50,000; at 60,000, 18 of 1,118 lost; at 80,000, 1,393 of 1,482 lost. All lines unique: fine at 100,000; at 150,000, 2,478 of 2,664 lost; at 200,000, 3,528 of 3,548. At about 400,000 characters nothing is indexed and all but one line is lost. Through the real editor in jsdom: Tab at 29,999 characters kept the word at its true offset; at 40,049 the record collapsed and styled nothing; one app undo restored it. Other edits on the one-line note: 20 scattered line edits lost 30 of 800 lines at 60,000 and 773 of 1,334 at 100,000. A change to the first and last lines held up to 200,000, the largest tested.
rejected: A budget across a whole reconcile: clients reconcile different batches and could stop converging
decisions.reason: The person asked at Gate 3 to record the remaining per-element limit. Convergence decides it: the bound must be a function of one element's two versions. At Gate 4 the person accepted the Tab limit on very long notes and asked for these numbers to be recorded. decisions.choice: sanitizeTextRanges(raw, originalText) is the single validator. restore.ts calls it, and every reader (getTextStyleRuns, the merge, the delta) calls it too, so bad data from any path is repaired or dropped and never thrown on. units.behaviour: Pure diff between two strings as hunks, and mapping of a range's start and end through those hunks.
rules: Exact constants at the top: const MIN_MATCH_LENGTH = 3; const MAX_MATCH_CANDIDATES = 16; const GRAM_INDEX_WORK = 4; const MIN_GRAM_TABLE_SIZE = 256; export const MAX_DIFF_WORK = 2_000_000; const WORD_CHARACTER = /[\p{L}\p{N}]/u;. MAX_DIFF_CELLS is gone. No clock, no randomness, no module state: a result depends only on the arguments, and meter is the only argument a function changes.

Types after TextHunk, which stays as it is and also describes a gap: export type DiffMeter = { left: number }; type TextBlock = { oldStart: number; newStart: number; length: number }; type GramIndex = { mask: number; starts: Int32Array; positions: Int32Array };
isHighSurrogate = (code: number) => code >= 0xd800 && code <= 0xdbff. isLowSurrogate = (code: number) => code >= 0xdc00 && code <= 0xdfff. Neither is exported.
getGramHash = (text: string, at: number, mask: number) => exactly (Math.imul((text.charCodeAt(at) << 11) ^ (text.charCodeAt(at + 1) << 5) ^ text.charCodeAt(at + 2), 0x9e3779b1) >>> 12) & mask.
buildGramIndex(text: string): GramIndex step 1: const count = text.length - MIN_MATCH_LENGTH + 1; let size = MIN_GRAM_TABLE_SIZE; while (size < count * 2) size *= 2; const mask = size - 1.

buildGramIndex step 2: const starts = new Int32Array(size + 1). For at from 0 to count - 1: starts[getGramHash(text, at, mask) + 1]++. Then for slot from 0 to size - 1: starts[slot + 1] += starts[slot].

buildGramIndex step 3: const positions = new Int32Array(count); const filled = starts.slice(0, size). For at from 0 to count - 1 in ascending order: positions[filled[getGramHash(text, at, mask)]++] = at. Return { mask, starts, positions }. One slot's positions are the entries from index starts[slot] up to but not including index starts[slot + 1], ascending. A slot can hold different grams; getLongerBlock compares real characters, so a collision only wastes one try.

getFirstAtOrAfter(positions: Int32Array, from: number, to: number, value: number): let low = from; let high = to; while (low < high) { const middle = (low + high) >>> 1; if positions[middle] < value then low = middle + 1, else high = middle }. Return low.

getLongerBlock(oldText: string, newText: string, gap: TextHunk, oldAt: number, newAt: number, best: TextBlock | null, meter: DiffMeter): TextBlock | null, step 1, backward: let back = 0; while oldAt - back > gap.oldStart and newAt - back > gap.newStart and oldText.charCodeAt(oldAt - back - 1) === newText.charCodeAt(newAt - back - 1), back++. Then meter.left -= back + 1.

getLongerBlock step 2: let oldStart = oldAt - back; let newStart = newAt - back; const bestLength = best ? best.length : MIN_MATCH_LENGTH - 1. Return best at once if oldStart + bestLength >= gap.oldEnd, or newStart + bestLength >= gap.newEnd, or oldText.charCodeAt(oldStart + bestLength) !== newText.charCodeAt(newStart + bestLength): a longer run must match at that offset, so this needs no scan.

getLongerBlock step 3, forward: let length = back; while oldStart + length < gap.oldEnd and newStart + length < gap.newEnd and oldText.charCodeAt(oldStart + length) === newText.charCodeAt(newStart + length), length++. Then meter.left -= length. Start from back and not from back + MIN_MATCH_LENGTH, because a slot can hold another gram.

getLongerBlock step 4, surrogates: if isLowSurrogate(oldText.charCodeAt(oldStart)) then oldStart++, newStart++ and length--. Then if length > 0 and isHighSurrogate(oldText.charCodeAt(oldStart + length - 1)) then length--. Return length > bestLength ? { oldStart, newStart, length } : best.

searchAt(oldText: string, newText: string, gap: TextHunk, index: GramIndex, newAt: number, found: TextBlock | null, meter: DiffMeter): TextBlock | null, step 1: meter.left -= 1; const { mask, starts, positions } = index; const slot = getGramHash(newText, newAt, mask); const first = starts[slot]; const end = starts[slot + 1]. If first === end return found.

searchAt step 2: const target = gap.oldStart + Math.floor(((newAt - gap.newStart) * (gap.oldEnd - gap.oldStart)) / (gap.newEnd - gap.newStart)), the old position on the gap's own diagonal. let right = getFirstAtOrAfter(positions, first, end, target); let left = right - 1; let best = found.

searchAt step 3: for (let tries = 0; tries < MAX_MATCH_CANDIDATES && meter.left > 0; tries++): const hasRight = right < end && positions[right] + MIN_MATCH_LENGTH <= gap.oldEnd; const hasLeft = left >= first && positions[left] >= gap.oldStart. If neither, break. const takeRight = hasRight && (!hasLeft || positions[right] - target <= target - positions[left]); const oldAt = takeRight ? positions[right++] : positions[left--]; best = getLongerBlock(oldText, newText, gap, oldAt, newAt, best, meter). After the loop return best.
getStride = (best: TextBlock | null) => (best ? best.length - 1 : 1). A run longer than best has a whole gram at each of best.length - 1 consecutive positions, so this step cannot skip it.

findLongestBlock(oldText: string, newText: string, gap: TextHunk, index: GramIndex, seed: TextBlock | null, meter: DiffMeter): TextBlock | null: let best = seed; const lastAt = gap.newEnd - MIN_MATCH_LENGTH; let right = Math.min(lastAt, (gap.newStart + gap.newEnd) >>> 1); let left = right - 1. while ((right <= lastAt || left >= gap.newStart) && meter.left > 0): if right <= lastAt then best = searchAt(oldText, newText, gap, index, right, best, meter) and right += getStride(best); if left >= gap.newStart then best = searchAt(oldText, newText, gap, index, left, best, meter) and left -= getStride(best). Return best. Moving outward from the middle is what makes a tie nearest the middle win, so a repetitive note splits in half each time.

trimHunk(oldText: string, newText: string, hunk: TextHunk, atStart: boolean, atEnd: boolean): TextHunk: let { oldStart, oldEnd, newStart, newEnd } = hunk. If atStart: while oldStart < oldEnd and newStart < newEnd and oldText[oldStart] === newText[newStart], oldStart++ and newStart++; then if oldStart > hunk.oldStart and isHighSurrogate(oldText.charCodeAt(oldStart - 1)), oldStart-- and newStart--. If atEnd: while oldStart < oldEnd and newStart < newEnd and oldText[oldEnd - 1] === newText[newEnd - 1], oldEnd-- and newEnd--; then if oldEnd < hunk.oldEnd and isLowSurrogate(oldText.charCodeAt(oldEnd)), oldEnd++ and newEnd++. Return { oldStart, oldEnd, newStart, newEnd }.

isInsideWord = (text: string, at: number): boolean => at > 0 && at < text.length && WORD_CHARACTER.test(text[at - 1]) && WORD_CHARACTER.test(text[at]). splitsSurrogatePair = (text: string, at: number): boolean => at > 0 && at < text.length && isHighSurrogate(text.charCodeAt(at - 1)) && isLowSurrogate(text.charCodeAt(at)). Neither is exported.

alignLines(oldText: string, newText: string, hunk: TextHunk): TextHunk[] | null: oldLines = oldText.slice(hunk.oldStart, hunk.oldEnd).split("\n"), newLines the same for the new side. Return null if oldLines.length < 2 or oldLines.length !== newLines.length. Otherwise walk the line pairs from hunk.oldStart and hunk.newStart. Each pair gives trimHunk(oldText, newText, { oldStart: oldAt, oldEnd, newStart: newAt, newEnd }, true, true), where oldEnd = oldAt + oldLines[i].length and newEnd = newAt + newLines[i].length, and then oldAt = oldEnd + 1 and newAt = newEnd + 1.

alignToken(oldText: string, newText: string, hunk: TextHunk): TextHunk[] | null: length = hunk.oldEnd - hunk.oldStart. Return null if length < 1, or length >= MIN_MATCH_LENGTH, or hunk.newEnd - hunk.newStart <= length, or isInsideWord(oldText, hunk.oldStart), or isInsideWord(oldText, hunk.oldEnd), or token = oldText.slice(hunk.oldStart, hunk.oldEnd) has token.trim() === "". For at from hunk.newStart while at + length <= hunk.newEnd: at the first at where newText.startsWith(token, at), neither at nor at + length is inside a word of newText, and neither splits a surrogate pair of newText, return the two insertions { oldStart: hunk.oldStart, oldEnd: hunk.oldStart, newStart: hunk.newStart, newEnd: at } and { oldStart: hunk.oldEnd, oldEnd: hunk.oldEnd, newStart: at + length, newEnd: hunk.newEnd }. Return null if there is none.

getSlide(changed: string, other: string, start: number, end: number, at: number, lower: number, upper: number): number: return 0 if !isInsideWord(other, at). let canLeft = true; let canRight = true. For step from 1 to end - start: canLeft = canLeft && start - step >= lower && changed[start - step] === changed[end - step]; if canLeft, at - step is not inside a word of other, and neither start - step nor end - step splits a surrogate pair of changed, return -step. canRight = canRight && end + step <= upper && changed[start + step - 1] === changed[end + step - 1]; if canRight, at + step is not inside a word of other, and neither start + step nor end + step splits a surrogate pair of changed, return step. Break when neither can move. Return 0. Left comes before right at each step, so a tie has one answer.

refineHunks(oldText: string, newText: string, hunks: readonly TextHunk[], meter: DiffMeter): TextHunk[], first loop: const aligned: TextHunk[] = []. For each hunk, with oldLength and newLength its two sides: if meter.left <= 0 or oldLength === 0 or newLength === 0, push the hunk and continue. meter.left -= oldLength + newLength. lines = alignLines(oldText, newText, hunk); if not null, aligned.push(...lines) and continue. token = alignToken(oldText, newText, hunk); if not null, aligned.push(...token) and continue. Push the hunk.

refineHunks second loop: parts = aligned with hunks empty on both sides filtered out. For each index i, with hunk = parts[i], isInsertion = hunk.oldStart === hunk.oldEnd and isDeletion = hunk.newStart === hunk.newEnd: skip it if meter.left <= 0 or it is neither. previous = parts[i - 1], next = parts[i + 1]. meter.left -= hunk.oldEnd - hunk.oldStart + (hunk.newEnd - hunk.newStart). slide = for an insertion getSlide(newText, oldText, hunk.newStart, hunk.newEnd, hunk.oldStart, previous ? previous.newEnd : 0, next ? next.newStart : newText.length), and for a deletion getSlide(oldText, newText, hunk.oldStart, hunk.oldEnd, hunk.newStart, previous ? previous.oldEnd : 0, next ? next.oldStart : oldText.length). If slide !== 0, parts[i] is the hunk with all four offsets moved by slide. Return parts.
diffText is export const diffText = (oldText: string, newText: string, meter: DiffMeter = { left: MAX_DIFF_WORK }): TextHunk[]. Step 1: if oldText === newText return [].

diffText step 2: const whole: TextHunk = { oldStart: 0, oldEnd: oldText.length, newStart: 0, newEnd: newText.length }; const trimmed = trimHunk(oldText, newText, whole, true, true); const indexWork = oldText.length * GRAM_INDEX_WORK + newText.length.

diffText step 5: const blocks: TextBlock[] = []; const queue: TextHunk[] = [whole]. for (let head = 0; head < queue.length && meter.left > 0; head++): const gap = queue[head]; const block = findLongestBlock(oldText, newText, gap, index, head === 0 ? seed : null, meter); if (!block) continue; blocks.push(block). The queue is read by index and never shifted, so gaps run breadth-first and there is no recursion.

If gap.oldEnd - oldAfter >= MIN_MATCH_LENGTH && gap.newEnd - newAfter >= MIN_MATCH_LENGTH, queue.push({ oldStart: oldAfter, oldEnd: gap.oldEnd, newStart: newAfter, newEnd: gap.newEnd }).

diffText step 8: const gaps: TextHunk[] = []; let oldAt = 0; let newAt = 0. For each block: gaps.push({ oldStart: oldAt, oldEnd: block.oldStart, newStart: newAt, newEnd: block.newStart }); oldAt = block.oldStart + block.length; newAt = block.newStart + block.length. After the last block: gaps.push({ oldStart: oldAt, oldEnd: oldText.length, newStart: newAt, newEnd: newText.length }).

Only those two gaps are trimmed, because a gap between two blocks has no common prefix or suffix left to give.

mapStart(p): delta = 0; for each hunk in order: if p < hunk.oldStart stop; if p <= hunk.oldEnd return hunk.newEnd; delta = hunk.newEnd - hunk.oldEnd. Return p + delta. So an insertion exactly at a range's start moves the start past the inserted text.

mapEnd(p): delta = 0; for each hunk in order: if p <= hunk.oldStart stop; if p <= hunk.oldEnd return hunk.newStart; delta = hunk.newEnd - hunk.oldEnd. Return p + delta. So an insertion exactly at a range's end leaves the end where it is.

units.behaviour: The range model: validation, resolving layers to disjoint style runs, local style and text operations.
rules: Imports: colorToHex, isTransparent, randomId from @excalidraw/common; hashString from "." (as textElement.ts imports from "."); diffText, mapSpanThroughHunks from ./textDiff; types from ./types. Exact constants: MAX_TEXT_RANGES = 1024 (exported), MAX_TEXT_RANGE_ID_LENGTH = 64, MAX_TEXT_RANGE_COLOR_LENGTH = 64.
isValidTextRangeColor: typeof value === "string", value.length <= 64, and colorToHex(value) !== null.

canonicalizeTextRanges: return a new array sorted by z ascending, then id ascending, comparing ids with < and > (never localeCompare). If longer than MAX_TEXT_RANGES keep only the last MAX_TEXT_RANGES entries.
Every record is written with keys in the order id, start, end, z, color, highlight, retired, origin, and with absent keys left out, not set to undefined.

areTextRangesEqual: both undefined is true, exactly one undefined is false, otherwise textHash equal, ranges lengths equal, and each index equal on id, start, end, z, color, highlight, retired and on every field of origin.

sanitizeTextRanges step 1: return undefined unless raw is an object with an array `ranges`. Return undefined if raw.textHash !== hashString(originalText). Read only the first MAX_TEXT_RANGES * 16 entries of ranges. Never throw.

sanitizeTextRanges step 2, per entry, dropping it if any check fails: it is a non-null object; id is a string of length 1 to 64 not already seen; start, end and z are integers (Number.isInteger); z >= 0; end >= start.
sanitizeTextRanges step 3: keep color only if it is null or isValidTextRangeColor, the same for highlight. Drop the entry if neither key remains.

sanitizeTextRanges step 4: clamp start and end to 0..originalText.length. Keep retired only when it is exactly true. Keep origin only when it is an object whose version and versionNonce are integers, whose text is a string, and whose start and end are integers with 0 <= start <= end <= text.length; otherwise leave it out.

sanitizeTextRanges step 5: keep a collapsed entry (start === end), with or without retired and origin: it is the tombstone of deleted characters, and restoreElements runs on every remote element before reconcile, so dropping it here would let a merge re-add it. Then canonicalizeTextRanges. Return undefined if nothing remains. If the result equals raw (areTextRangesEqual) return raw itself, else return { textHash: raw.textHash, ranges }.
getTextStyleRuns step 1: textRanges = sanitizeTextRanges(element.textRanges, element.originalText); return [] if undefined. Use only records that are not retired and have start < end.
getTextStyleRuns step 2: for each of the attributes color and highlight build a list of records with that key present, sorted by z descending, then null values before strings, then id descending.

getTextStyleRuns step 3: bounds = sorted unique start and end values of the used records. For each consecutive pair [a, b) take, for each attribute, the first record in its list with start <= a and end >= b. Its value is the style, and no record or a null value means null.
getTextStyleRuns step 4: skip segments where both attributes are null, join adjacent segments with equal color and highlight, and return runs ascending. Runs are disjoint.

applyTextRangeStyle step 1: clamp span to 0..originalText.length, returning element.textRanges if start >= end. Normalize style: an attribute with a transparent string (isTransparent) becomes null; an attribute that is undefined or an invalid string is left out. Return element.textRanges if neither attribute remains.

applyTextRangeStyle step 2: current = sanitizeTextRanges(element.textRanges, element.originalText)?.ranges ?? []; z = 1 + the highest z in current, or 1 if empty. Every existing record loses its origin.

applyTextRangeStyle step 3, a removal: a record r is removed by this style when it is not retired, r.start < end and r.end > start (so a collapsed record never qualifies), it has at least one string attribute, and each of its string attributes is one whose value in style is null. A colour or highlight pick has no null, so it removes nothing, and a clear record has no string attribute, so it is never removed. Set retired: true on every removed r, keeping its offsets. If r.start < start, add a kept part { id: randomId(), start: r.start, end: start, z: r.z } with r's color and highlight keys as they are. If r.end > end, add a kept part { id: randomId(), start: end, end: r.end, z: r.z } the same way. A kept part never has retired or origin.
applyTextRangeStyle step 4: add { id: randomId(), start, end, z, ...style }. next = { textHash: hashString(element.originalText), ranges: canonicalizeTextRanges(all) }.

applyTextRangeStyle step 5: if getTextStyleRuns of the element and of { originalText, textRanges: next } are field-for-field equal, return element.textRanges, so a no-op adds nothing and an element that never had ranges stays without the key (FR-2). Otherwise return next.

shiftTextRanges step 1: return textRanges if it is undefined or oldText === newText. current = sanitizeTextRanges(textRanges, oldText); if undefined return textRanges unchanged, which stays stale and ignored.

shiftTextRanges step 2: hunks = diffText(oldText, newText), computed once. Map each record through mapSpanThroughHunks. Drop origin from every record. Keep every record whatever its span: a record whose span collapses stays collapsed and native, which is what stops a merge re-adding it from a peer's copy, and stops old text reaching origin (FR-3). Return { textHash: hashString(newText), ranges: canonicalizeTextRanges(mapped) }.

getTextRangesUpdate: return {} if element.textRanges is undefined or nextOriginalText === element.originalText; otherwise { textRanges: shiftTextRanges(element.originalText, nextOriginalText, element.textRanges) }.

units.behaviour: The pure, symmetric merge of two versions' ranges, and how a history delta is applied to ranges.
rules: Imports: randomId from @excalidraw/common; hashString from "."; isTextElement from ./typeChecks; MAX_DIFF_WORK, diffText, mapSpanThroughHunks from ./textDiff; types DiffMeter and TextHunk from ./textDiff; areTextRangesEqual, canonicalizeTextRanges, sanitizeTextRanges, shiftTextRanges from ./textRanges.

One const meter: DiffMeter = { left: MAX_DIFF_WORK } and one hunksByText Map, both declared before the loop, serve every record of that call. This file holds no diff constant of its own.
mergeTextRanges must read no clock, random source or module state and must never mutate its inputs. randomId is used only by applyTextRangesDelta.

mergeTextRanges step 1: return base if either element is not a text element, or if neither has textRanges. Elements with no ranges therefore reconcile as today, and the same object comes back (FR-20).
mergeTextRanges step 2: baseRanges = sanitizeTextRanges(base.textRanges, base.originalText)?.ranges ?? [], otherRanges = the same for other. Return base if otherRanges is empty.
getRegister(record, element) = record.origin ?? { version: element.version, versionNonce: element.versionNonce, text: element.originalText, start: record.start, end: record.end }.

pickNewerRegister(a, b): higher version wins; at equal version lower versionNonce wins; at equal nonce the smaller of (text, start, end) compared in that order wins, so a result is defined even for crafted input.

mergeTextRanges step 3, for every id in the union with bRec and oRec being its records: id, z, color and highlight come from bRec ?? oRec. retired is true if either side is retired, otherwise the key stays absent.

mergeTextRanges step 4, the position: if bRec exists and has no origin, use bRec.start and bRec.end with no origin. Otherwise register = pickNewerRegister over the registers of the records present, using base for bRec and other for oRec.

mergeTextRanges step 5: if register.version === base.version and register.versionNonce === base.versionNonce and register.text === base.originalText, use register.start and register.end with no origin. Otherwise read hunks = hunksByText.get(register.text); on a miss, hunks = diffText(register.text, base.originalText, meter) and hunksByText.set(register.text, hunks), so each distinct text is paid for once. Use mapSpanThroughHunks(hunks, register.start, register.end) and set origin to register, whose fields are never changed.

mergeTextRanges step 6: keep collapsed records, never drop one here. ranges = canonicalizeTextRanges(records), next = { textHash: hashString(base.originalText), ranges }. If areTextRangesEqual(next, base.textRanges) return base. Otherwise return { ...base, textRanges: next }, built with a spread and not newElementWith, which would bump the version.

applyTextRangesDelta step 1: holdsText = typeof inserted.originalText === "string"; nextText = holdsText ? inserted.originalText : element.originalText; prior = sanitizeTextRanges(element.textRanges, element.originalText)?.ranges ?? [].

applyTextRangesDelta step 2: if nextText !== element.originalText, shifted = shiftTextRanges(element.originalText, nextText, element.textRanges)?.ranges ?? []; otherwise shifted = prior. Put shifted into a Map by id.

applyTextRangesDelta step 3: priorAlive = ids of deleted.textRanges?.ranges that are not retired, targetAlive = the same for inserted.textRanges?.ranges. Read these two arrays directly with Array.isArray, since a delta is local history data.
applyTextRangesDelta step 4: for each id in priorAlive and not in targetAlive, if the Map has it, set a copy with retired: true.

applyTextRangesDelta step 5: for each record t of inserted.textRanges?.ranges that is not retired and whose id is not in priorAlive, in array order: let c = Map.get(t.id). If c exists and is not retired, skip it. The span is t's when holdsText, else c's if c exists, else t's, clamped to 0..nextText.length. If c is retired, add a new record with id: randomId(), the span, t's z, and t's color and highlight, so undoing a removal restores the layer order. If c is absent, add t without origin, with the span.

applyTextRangesDelta step 6: exact = holdsText and deleted.originalText === element.originalText. addressed = inserted.textRanges?.textHash === hashString(nextText). For each non-retired t in inserted.textRanges?.ranges whose Map entry exists and is not retired, set that entry's start and end to t's, clamped, when exact is true, or when addressed is true and both the entry and the record of the same id in deleted.textRanges?.ranges are collapsed (start === end). The first restores exact offsets when no other text change came in between. The second gives a word its range back when the step being undone is the one that lost the word, because t's offsets address that text. Any other collapsed record stays collapsed (FR-3).

applyTextRangesDelta step 7: next = { textHash: hashString(nextText), ranges: canonicalizeTextRanges(Map values) }. If element.textRanges is undefined and ranges is empty return undefined. If areTextRangesEqual(next, element.textRanges) return element.textRanges. Otherwise return next.

units.behaviour: Maps style runs onto rendered lines without measuring, and lays one line's runs out as positioned pieces for canvas and SVG.
rules: Imports: hasRTLChars from @excalidraw/common; getTextStyleRuns from ./textRanges; types from ./types. No canvas or DOM use in this file: widths come only from the measure argument, so it stays testable and usable with a non-DOM canvas.

getRenderedLineOffsets, purpose: element.text is originalText with soft line breaks added, trailing whitespace dropped at soft breaks, and tokens of wrapped lines normalized to NFC. It returns, for each line of text, one source offset per code unit plus one final entry for the line's end.

getRenderedLineOffsets step 1: lines = text.replace(/
?/g, "
").split("
"); p = 0. For each line, walk j from 0 while j < line.length.

getRenderedLineOffsets step 2: while p < originalText.length and originalText[p] !== line[j]: match /^[\s\S]\p{M}+/u against originalText.slice(p, p + 32). If it matches and line.startsWith(cluster.normalize("NFC"), j), push p once per code unit of the normalized cluster, add its length to j, add the cluster's length to p, and go back to step 1's loop. Otherwise, if originalText[p] matches /\s/, p += 1. Otherwise return null.
getRenderedLineOffsets step 3: if p >= originalText.length with j still < line.length return null. Otherwise push p, then p += 1 and j += 1. After the line, push p as its final entry.

getTextLineRuns step 1: runs = getTextStyleRuns(element); return null if empty. lineOffsets = getRenderedLineOffsets(element.text, element.originalText); return null if null, so a text out of step with its source renders unstyled, never wrongly styled.

getTextLineRuns step 2: for each rendered line, walk its code units with a pointer into runs (offsets never decrease). Group contiguous code units with the same color and highlight into { start, end, text, color, highlight }, where start and end are offsets into the rendered line and a unit in no run has color and highlight null. Never start a new group on a low surrogate (0xDC00 to 0xDFFF): it stays with the unit before it.

getTextLineRuns step 3: an empty line, or a line whose groups all have null color and null highlight, is null in the result, which means draw it as today. Return null if every line is null. The result has one entry per rendered line.

layoutTextLine step 1, directional segments: if direction is "ltr" and !hasRTLChars(line) there is one ltr segment. Otherwise classify each code point: rtl if hasRTLChars(char), ltr if /[\p{L}\p{N}]/u matches, else neutral. A maximal run of neutrals takes the class of the strong characters on both sides when they agree, else direction; a missing side counts as direction. Group consecutive equal classes into segments { start, end, direction }.

layoutTextLine step 2, visual order: walk segments in logical order for ltr and reversed for rtl, with x = 0. Each segment gets x and width = measure(line.slice(start, end)); x += width. The layout's width is the final x.

layoutTextLine step 3, pieces: for each run in logical order and each segment it overlaps, in logical order, take [a, b) as the overlap. In an ltr segment piece.x = segment.x + measure(line.slice(segment.start, a)). In an rtl segment piece.x = segment.x + segment.width - measure(line.slice(segment.start, b)). piece.width = measure(line.slice(a, b)), piece.text = line.slice(a, b), piece.direction = segment.direction, color and highlight from the run.
getTextLineLeft: "center" gives (elementWidth - lineWidth) / 2, "right" gives elementWidth - lineWidth, anything else 0.

units.behaviour: The preview layer behind the textarea: shows each run's colour and highlight, aligned with the textarea, and exists only while the element has visible runs.
rules: Imports: applyDarkModeFilter from @excalidraw/common; type TextStyleRun from @excalidraw/element. ownerDocument is editable.ownerDocument.
Exact constant: PREVIEW_CLASS_NAME = "excalidraw-wysiwyg-preview", exported.

Exact mirrored style keys, in this order, as a const array: position, display, minHeight, margin, padding, border, zIndex, wordBreak, whiteSpace, overflowWrap, boxSizing, backfaceVisibility, font, fontFamily, lineHeight, width, height, left, top, transformOrigin, transform, textAlign, verticalAlign, opacity. font comes before fontFamily and lineHeight, because setting font resets them.
update with an empty runs list: if the node is attached, remove it. Call editable.style.removeProperty("caret-color"). Return. The caller has already set the textarea's normal colour.

update with runs, step 1: create the node once, as a div with className PREVIEW_CLASS_NAME, aria-hidden="true", dir="auto", and fixed styles pointerEvents none, userSelect none, overflow hidden, background transparent, unicodeBidi plaintext (the textarea's dir="auto" makes each paragraph plaintext).

update with runs, step 2: copy each mirrored key from editable.style to the node's style. Set node.style.color = baseColor, editable.style.caretColor = baseColor, editable.style.color = "transparent".

update with runs, step 3: key = JSON.stringify([editable.value, runs, isDark]). When it differs from the last key, rebuild the children: walk runs over editable.value; text outside a run is a text node; a run is a <span> whose textContent is the slice, with style.color = applyDarkModeFilter(run.color, isDark) when color is set and style.backgroundColor = applyDarkModeFilter(run.highlight, isDark) when highlight is set. Use createElement, createTextNode and element.style only, never innerHTML.
update with runs, step 4: if the node has no parent, parent?.insertBefore(node, editable.parentNode === parent ? editable : null), so the textarea stays on top. Then syncScroll.
syncScroll: if the node exists, set node.scrollTop = editable.scrollTop and node.scrollLeft = editable.scrollLeft. It is an arrow function, so it can be assigned to editable.onscroll directly.
destroy: remove the node if attached and drop it.

exports.name: TextPreview
exports.returns: { update: (args: { runs: readonly TextStyleRun[]; baseColor: string; isDark: boolean }) => void; syncScroll: () => void; destroy: () => void }

rules: Import from ../src/textDiff and ../src/textRanges; hashString from ../src/index. Build elements as plain { originalText, textRanges } objects. T = "Bid request timeout 120ms", where "120ms" is [20, 25). RED = "#e03131", BLUE = "#1971c2", YELLOW = "#ffec99".
Seed a range with applyTextRangeStyle({ originalText: T }, { start: 20, end: 25 }, { color: RED }). Assert offsets through textRanges.ranges and getTextStyleRuns, never on an id value.

Fixtures, text: const PROSE = "Bid request timeout 120ms applies to every exchange in the primary region. When the auction server misses that window the request is dropped and the slot is sold through the fallback path. Review the latency dashboard before changing this value, and tell the on-call engineer about any change that touches the pricing service."; const ADDED = "Before the next release the team agreed to review every setting that controls how long a request may wait, and to write down who owns each one. The list below is the current state of that work, and it will change as the review goes on through the rest of the quarter, so please read it again before you rely on any of these numbers. "; (it ends with a space and is 333 characters; ADDED.slice(0, 100) is the 100-character form). const DIGITS = Array.from({ length: 2500 }, (_, i) => String(i).padStart(4, "0")).join(""); const seeded = (length: number, seed: number) => { let state = seed; let out = ""; for (let i = 0; i < length; i++) { state = (state * 1103515245 + 12345) & 0x7fffffff; out += String.fromCharCode(97 + ((state >>> 16) % 26)); } return out; }; const W = seeded(10_000, 12345);

Fixtures, helpers: const repeatTo = (text: string, length: number) => { let out = ""; while (out.length < length) { out += `${text} `; } return out.slice(0, length); }; const proseNote = (lineCount: number) => { const lines: string[] = []; let at = 0; while (lines.length < lineCount) { lines.push(PROSE.slice(at, at + 58).trim()); at = (at + 58) % (PROSE.length - 60); } return lines.join("
"); }; const digitNote = (lineCount: number) => Array.from({ length: lineCount }, (_, i) => DIGITS.slice(i * 60, i * 60 + 58)).join("
"); const indentAll = (text: string) => text.split("
").map((line) => `    ${line}`).join("
"); const spansOf = (text: string): [number, number][] => [...text.matchAll(/[^\s]+/g)].map((match) => [match.index!, match.index! + match[0].length]); const applyHunks = (oldText: string, newText: string, hunks: readonly TextHunk[]) => { let out = ""; let at = 0; for (const hunk of hunks) { out += oldText.slice(at, hunk.oldStart) + newText.slice(hunk.newStart, hunk.newEnd); at = hunk.oldEnd; } return out + oldText.slice(at); };

units.behaviour: Tests of concurrent edits: carrying in both arrival orders, no stale offsets, convergence across clients, removals staying removed, and a remote update dropped while editing. Also the diff budget, the meter's charges, and the final diff pass.
rules: Helpers: T = "Bid request timeout 120ms", W = `Urgent: ${T}`, RED = "#e03131". version(element, text, version, versionNonce) returns { ...element, originalText: text, text, version, versionNonce, index: "a0" }. run(local, remote, appState = {}) returns reconcileElements(cloneJSON([local]), cloneJSON([remote]) as RemoteExcalidrawElement[], appState as AppState)[0]. Text changes on a version go through shiftTextRanges when that version already has ranges.

A range edit is { ...element, textRanges: applyTextRangeStyle(element, span, style), version, versionNonce } built by spreading, so the test sets version and nonce itself. Lower versionNonce wins a tie, as in reconcile today.

sync(local, remote) is the path Collab._reconcileElements takes after restore: existing = cloneJSON([local]); return bumpElementVersions(reconcileElements(existing, cloneJSON([remote]) as RemoteExcalidrawElement[], {} as AppState), existing)[0]. bumpElementVersions comes from ../../data/restore. Never assert a bumped versionNonce's value, which is random: spread a fixed versionNonce over a bumped element where a test needs to know who wins next.

Client convergence is expect(a).toEqual(b) on whole elements, so version, versionNonce, originalText and textRanges must all agree. Between run calls that holds at once. After sync, the two clients of an equal-version race differ in version, versionNonce and updated until the next delivery, so before it assert originalText and textRanges only, and after it assert whole elements.

The test "a meter pays for the whole run it reads". Why this input: the exact spent tests above never reach meter.left -= length, because each pair has no common run, or a run the trim's seed already holds, so every candidate returns at the bestLength check. units.behaviour: Tests that ranges survive bound-text containers, font changes, list markers, and undo and redo.
rules: Setup: beforeEach await render(<Excalidraw handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />). Seed ranges with newElementWith(text, { textRanges: applyTextRangeStyle(text, span, style) }) before API.setElements, never with mutateElement. RED = "#e03131", T = "Bid request timeout 120ms", W = `Urgent: ${T}`.

History: put the starting element in with API.updateScene({ elements: [element], captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY }), edit through the text editor as in U30, leave with Keyboard.exitTextEditor(editor), then use Keyboard.undo() and Keyboard.redo(). A remote change is API.updateScene({ elements, captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER }).

After every history step assert the check noStale(element): for each run of getTextStyleRuns(element), element.originalText.slice(run.start, run.end) is the expected word, and sanitizeTextRanges(element.textRanges, element.originalText) is defined.
